faq.a: A mirage is a real image made when layers of air at different temperatures bend light. It makes things appear in the wrong place, like the sky appearing on a hot road as a shimmering puddle.

faq.q: Why does hot air bend light?
faq.a: Light travels slightly faster in hot, thin air than in cooler, denser air. When light passes at a slant between air of different temperatures, it changes direction, which is called refraction.

faq.q: Is a mirage real or in my head?
faq.a: A mirage is real light, not a hallucination, so you can photograph it. What is wrong is your brain's guess about where the light came from.
asks: Can you take a photo of a mirage?

faq.q: Why does the puddle disappear when I get closer?
faq.a: The bent light only reaches your eyes at a very shallow angle from far away. As you get nearer, you look down more steeply and the bent sky light no longer reaches you.
asks: Why does a mirage move away from you?
Why can I never reach the puddle?

faq.a: The hot air above the road is constantly rising and mixing in little bubbles. This makes the bending change from moment to moment, so the fake puddle wobbles and shimmers.
asks: Why does air look wavy over a hot road?
Why do things wobble above a fire?

facts: A mirage on a hot road is called an inferior mirage because the image appears below the real object, the sky.
Mirages are real images formed by refraction, so they can be photographed.

quiz.why: Hot air near the road bends sky light up into your eyes, so you see a patch of sky on the road that looks like water.

wrong.0: There is no water there; the puddle moves away as you approach.
wrong.2: Oil does not move away or vanish as you get closer.
